newsitem.title: POLAND: Italian publisher to sell Polish daily stake.
newsitem.headline: Italian publisher to sell Polish daily stake.

text.p: The Italian company publishing the Il Sole 24 Ore business daily will sell its 51 stake in Polish economic newspaper Nowa Europa to the paper's other shareholder, a Nowa Europa official said on Wednesday.
"The agreement on the sale should soon be signed," the paper's deputy editor-in-chief Zbigniew Maciag told Reuters.
He declined to name the sum to be paid for the stake.
After the sale, the Nowa Europa, in circulation since 1992, will be fully owned by Infor Publishers, a Polish company publishing 27 periodicals, mainly economic and legal ones.

Infor's owner Ryszard Pienkowski has said he plans to merge the loss-making Nowa Europa with one of this other papers, either the Gazeta Prawna or the Legal Gazette, to increase circulation and strengthen its position on the market.
He said he wanted the new title to reach a circulation of at least 90,000 copies daily, which is the number of copies sold by the Gazeta Prawna, published twice a week and providing legal advice.
The Nowa Europa, now published in some 45,000 copies, sells only half of them.

Pienkowski was quoted by the Gazeta Wyborcza daily on Wednesday as saying that the merger was meant to ready the two papers for competition from Swedish company Bonnier, which has launched a new business daily called the Puls Biznesu (the Pulse of Business).
